# [TASK] Frontend: Recommendations view/section

## Task
Build the Recommendations view/section rendering ranked, explained results.

## Scope
Presentation only — consumes Task #220's hook.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] New view, following existing `MovieList`/`Movie` component conventions and styling (`Recommendations.jsx` at route `/recommendations`, `Recommendations.test.jsx`)
- [x] Each result shows ai-service's explanation text, not just a bare movie card, per #196 AC4 (`Movie.jsx`'s new optional `caption` prop; `Recommendations.test.jsx: "renders each recommendation with its ai-service explanation text..."` and `"hydrates each card by its own movieId, keeping title and reason correctly paired"`)
- [x] Empty state (no history) and error state each render distinct, clear UI — no blank screen either way (`Recommendations.test.jsx`: the isEmpty, error, "zero picks", and pre-fetch-uninitialized-tick tests, each asserting the other branches' text is absent)
- [x] Loading state matches the existing skeleton/spinner convention used elsewhere in the app (`CircularProgress`, same as `Movies.jsx`; `Recommendations.test.jsx: "shows a centered spinner..."`)

## Estimate
**Hours:** 5

## Notes
Reused `Movie.jsx` rather than duplicating its card markup: added an optional `caption` prop (renders under the rating, only when passed) instead of a second near-identical component — the three existing callers (`MovieList`, `RatedCards`) are unaffected. Sidebar gained an auth-gated "Recommendations" link (favorites, and so recommendations, are per-account).

The brief RTK Query tick right after `skip` flips to false (`isFetching: false`, `data`/`error` both still `undefined`) fell through to the zero-recommendations branch instead of showing the spinner; fixed to show the spinner during that tick.

If every card in a non-empty result has its own TMDB detail lookup fail, the view falls back to an empty grid under the "Recommended For You" heading rather than a message. `RatedCards.jsx` has the same limitation for favorites/watchlist. A real API failure is caught earlier, by #220's error state.
